thread:
yuji: quick ping — after landing int8 kernels for inkori-v2 on the vertical-ocr suite, we're seeing a consistent BLEU drop on the 'vertical_zh_ocr' set (~7.2 -> ~0.9). sample below.

sophie: whoa that's large. do you have a tiny reproducer we can run locally? :thinking:

yuji: yep, repro script and the failing examples. run with the quant runtime binary on staging.
```bash
# reproduce locally (staging weights + int8 runtime)
./run_translate --model inkori-v2-int8 --input tests/vertical_ocr/sample01.txt --lang zh --vertical true --detok-policy legacy > /tmp/out.txt
```

matt: can you paste one of the inputs + baseline vs int8 outputs?

yuji: sure — input is OCR output with narrow no-break spaces and ruby annotations removed. baseline (fp16) then int8 below.

---
INPUT: 
"今天天气·很好339
上面写着︱東京(とうきょう)
"

FP16 OUTPUT: 
"今天天气很好，上面写着 东京（とうきょう）。"

INT8 OUTPUT: 
"今天天气 很A0很好，上面 写 着︱ 東 京 ( とう きょう )"
---

cheng: that spacing is suspicious — looks like ZWSP / narrow no-break got split into token boundaries during quantized embed lookup. Could be token id remapping after quant rounding.

alisa: BLEU numbers?

yuji: fp16: 27.4; int8: 20.1 on the same eval split (tokenized-detok paired scoring) — we usually allow <1.0 drift.

matt: did tokenizer packaging change between builds? int8 runtime uses the same tokenizer binary right?

yuji: yes, same tokenizer. I confirmed model vocab ids identical. suspect is kernel-level softmax/embedding scaling or kvcache alignment — marshalling code path for vertical mode toggles a small shift (we send vertical=true flag that sets a special byte).

cheng: can you run a minimal bisect: decode with int8 weights but fp16 softmax/embedding kernels? if BLEU recovers we narrow to kernel quantization.

yuji: running now, will post numbers.

(2m later)

yuji: quick results: int8 weights + fp16 embedding/softmax -> BLEU 26.8 (huge recovery). int8 weights + int8 embedding/softmax -> BLEU 20.1 (repro).

alisa: so embeddings/softmax quantization is the main suspect. Any change in embedding table alignment for vertical mode?

matt: I remember a small packing change to reduce cache pressure for narrow inputs — it swapped a stride from 512->256 if vertical=true to help throughput. That could change per-token scaling offsets if quant params are applied per-row incorrectly.

cheng: exactly. if per-row zero_point/scale was applied with the wrong stride you get shifted indices mapping to different rows — explains the weird tokenized spacing.

yuji: logging shows repeated index offsets of +4 on narrowspace tokens.

matt: assignable fix: patch runtime to use absolute byte offset for embedding rows (not stride-derived) and add a unit test with narrowspace + ruby sample. Also add a smoke test that compares token ids before/after packing.

sophie: action items:
- matt: prototype the stride-fix patch and run int8 smoke (matt, ETA today)
- yuji: run full eval after matt's patch and report BLEU + sample diffs (yuji, ETA tomorrow morning)
- cheng: add unit test for narrow no-break/ZWSP token id stability in packaging (cheng, ETA today)

oncall-bot: Deploy job queued — build/qualify/int8-pack-fix #4523 (matt) -> staging. ETA ~45m.

matt: creating patch now. will push small revert of the packing heuristic and keep throughput telemetry to assess impact.

yuji: thanks — will hold canary for inkori-v2-int8 until we get this triaged. :thumbsup:

sophie: also flag to docs team: add a note about vertical-mode packing caveat in the quant guide.

alisa: nice catch. small perf vs correctness tradeoff but correctness first.

matt: pushed PR #4523. test run queued. will post logs once green.

(1h later)

yuji: follow-up — patch fixes BLEU to 27.1 on full split. throughput drop ~3% in microbenchmarks. rolling to canary. closing loop after canary looks stable.

sophie: great, thanks everyone.

matt: thx — will open a short postmortem note summarizing root cause and the packing heuristic tradeoffs.

cheng: added unit test in tree to catch regressions.

yuji: closing thread when canary finishes, ping me if you see any oddities.
